items.how: Make the status resolve to Ready or Not ready, or to an error with a retry. Show a message when the check times out. Do not leave the Check if ready button disabled with no explanation. Acceptance: after the check, the reader sees a result or a message within a bounded time, and the button is usable again.
items.why: o1.png and s1.png both show 'Status: Checking...' with a greyed-out Check if ready button and no result, so the reader cannot learn whether the book is ready. This is the release goal's second step. Both reviewers also rate the story broken.

items.how: The Captain decides whether a reader gets their own collect action or collecting stays a desk-staff action. If staff-only, the reader view should say so (for example 'Show this at the front desk') and the release goal wording should be corrected. If readers collect, add a collect action to the reader view.
items.why: s3.png shows the reader view reading 'Ready at the front desk' with only a Back button and no way to collect. o-collect.png shows Collect (staff only) in the desk-staff view. The release goal says 'a reader can ... collect it', but the product may intend staff to do the collecting, so who owns the step is a product call.

sides.why: o signed in as desk staff, so o-collect.png tests a different persona from the release's reader.

sides.position: no way to collect as a reader
sides.why: s3.png matches the release persona and shows no collect control. What it shows is that the reader sees no instruction either.

items.how: Keep the Reserve button visible at 1366x768, for example in a sticky action bar or after a shorter form. For keyboard users, put the primary action early in the tab order or add a skip link. Acceptance: at 1366x768 the Reserve button is on screen without scrolling.
items.why: o2.png and s2.png show a five-field form filling the window with the window's bottom edge at 1366x768 and no Reserve button visible. The story still completes and the person can scroll, so this is friction, not a block. The walk did not test resize.

items.how: Use one label for the action across the reservation list and the form. Acceptance: the same wording appears on the list button and on the form title and button.
items.why: o3.png shows 'Hold a book' on the reservation list and o2.png titles the form 'Reserve a copy', which confirms two names for one action. No step is blocked, but a reader may take them for two different actions.

items.how: Measure load time on staging with a real timing run. Rule it only if the measured time is a problem. Owner: the Captain.
items.why: s4.png shows a fully loaded page and carries no timings, so the ten-second claim is a feeling no picture settles. o did not report slowness.

deferred.how: Fold it into the i1 fix. Acceptance for i1 must also cover a readiness status that never shows stale data after the check returns.
deferred.why: o saw it and s agrees. The check-ready screen in o1.png and s1.png is already stuck on Checking, so the status is unreliable. A stale read on that same status would mislead a reader about whether the book is ready, so it is not worth deferring on its own.

deferred.how: Settle the long button label together with the i4 label unification.
deferred.why: o disagreed ('blocks me') but the picture o2.png shows the block comes from the button being below the fold, not from its length. That is i3. s agrees it is polish. The label itself is not visible in any picture, so it stays polish and rides with i4.

deferred.how: Check the decline against the declaration at x.d.ts: look for a prop or slot on Button that can supply it, and for a plugin-built part that can. If one exists, overrule the decline. If only a custom build can do it, the Captain decides whether to depart from the host's look.
deferred.why: The decline cites a host component and a path, but this pass reads no source and no picture shows the control. o said 'fine' without a picture and s said 'cannot tell, no picture', so nothing here upholds it.

tasks.scope: Captain rules whether the reader or desk staff collects. Then add a reader-view collect action or a staff-at-desk instruction, and align the release goal wording.
